blocks.content: It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.

rows: Non-justiciable (cannot be directly enforced by courts)
Available to citizens, and some extended to foreigners
Applicable strictly to citizens of India only
Added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) and 86th Amendment (2002)
Inspired by the Bill of Rights in the US Constitution
Inspired by the Constitution of the former USSR

items: Swaran Singh Committee originally recommended 8 Fundamental Duties, but the 42nd Amendment Act incorporated 10 duties.
The 11th Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(k) mandates parents/guardians to provide education opportunities to children aged 6 to 14 years.
Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable and non-self-executing, but Parliament can enact legislation to enforce them (e.g., Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971).
Unlike certain Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties apply strictly to Indian citizens and do not extend to foreigners.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Fundamental Duties were incorporated into Part IV-A of the Constitution under Article 51A by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
The inclusion of Fundamental Duties was based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee formed in 1976.
Originally, 10 Fundamental Duties were added; the 11th duty was incorporated by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act in 2002.
Fundamental Duties were inspired by the Constitution of the former USSR.
These duties serve as a constant reminder to citizens that while enjoying rights, they must also perform moral and civic responsibilities toward the nation.
